engine: WISER Reborn 2.6 Ultimate HazMat Sentinel (Standalone Offline PWA Snapshot)

chemicals.name: 2-Diethylaminoethanol (Boiler Corrosion Inhibitor)
chemicals.ppe_level: Butyl gloves, splash goggles, face shield
chemicals.symptoms: Severe corneal burns, 'halo vision', asthma-like bronchospasm, skin burns.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Flush eyes/skin 20 min. 2. Oxygen.
chemicals.fire_response: Alcohol-resistant foam, dry chemical, CO2.
chemicals.reactivity: Reacts exothermically with acids, oxidizers, and isocyanates.
chemicals.storage_temp: Corrosive Base / Flammable storage
chemicals.sds_key_points: Common steam-boiler treatment chemical in hospitals and schools.

chemicals.name: Acetone (Dimethyl Ketone)
chemicals.synonyms: 2-Propanone, Nail polish remover, Fiberglass resin cleaner
chemicals.odor: Fragrant, mint-like sweet fruity ketone odor
chemicals.ppe_level: Butyl rubber gloves (Acetone penetrates Nitrile in <5 minutes!) + goggles
chemicals.symptoms: Eye irritation, narcosis, dizziness, ketosis. Low toxicity compared to other solvents, but extreme flash fire hazard!
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Fresh air. 2. Flush eyes 15 min. 3. Wash skin.
chemicals.fire_response: Use Alcohol-Resistant Foam (AR-AFFF), dry chemical, or CO2. Standard hydrocarbon foam is destroyed by water-miscible acetone!
chemicals.reactivity: NEVER mix with Hydrogen Peroxide + Acid (forms shock-sensitive primary high explosive TATP!) or Chloroform + Base.
chemicals.storage_temp: Grounded Flammable Cabinet away from Peroxides
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Hydrogen peroxide, nitric/sulfuric acid, chloroform, chromic anhydride
chemicals.sds_key_points: Dissolves ABS plastic and permeates Nitrile gloves rapidly—use Butyl rubber!

chemicals.name: Acetonitrile (Methyl Cyanide)
chemicals.symptoms: 3 to 12 HOUR DELAYED CYANIDE POISONING as liver cytochrome P450 slowly converts Acetonitrile into free Cyanide! Initial nausea/headache followed hours later by lactic acidosis, seizures, and arrest.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Mandatory 24-hour ICU observation even if patient looks fine initially! 2. Administer CYANOKIT (Hydroxocobalamin) or Sodium Thiosulfate when lactate rises.
chemicals.antidote: Hydroxocobalamin (Cyanokit 5g IV) + Sodium Thiosulfate (watch for 3-12h delayed onset!).
chemicals.fire_response: Alcohol-resistant foam (AR-AFFF), CO2, dry chemical. Burns releasing HCN gas.
chemicals.reactivity: Reacts violently with nitric acid, sulfuric acid, perchlorates, and strong oxidizers.
chemicals.storage_temp: Grounded Flammable Cabinet
chemicals.sds_key_points: Biotech & analytical lab staple. Causes delayed Cyanide poisoning 3 to 12 hours after exposure!

chemicals.name: Acetylene, Dissolved
chemicals.physical_state: Gas (dissolved in acetone inside porous cylinder)
chemicals.respirator_req: SCBA in fire or high concentration
chemicals.symptoms: Simple asphyxiant; dizziness, headache, garlic breath; extreme explosive blast injury from cylinder decomposition.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Move to fresh air. 2. Administer oxygen. 3. Treat flash burns.
chemicals.fire_response: UNSTABLE GAS! Can decompose explosively without oxygen above 15 psi. If cylinder heats up, evacuate 800m and cool with unmanned monitor for 1+ hour after flame out.
chemicals.reactivity: Forms shock-sensitive explosive acetylides with copper (>65% Cu brass), silver, or mercury. Explodes on contact with chlorine.
chemicals.storage_temp: Chain upright in ventilated welding bay; minimum 20 ft from Oxygen
chemicals.sds_key_points: Shop oxy-acetylene torch gas. Never open regulator above 15 psig.

chemicals.name: Acrylonitrile, Stabilized
chemicals.hazard_class: 3 / 6.1 (Flammable Liquid, Poison - Releases Cyanide in Body)
chemicals.color: Clear colorless to pale yellow liquid
chemicals.ppe_level: Level A Suit + SCBA (absorbs rapidly through leather and rubber!)
chemicals.symptoms: Metabolizes to CYANIDE in vivo! Headache, asphyxia, seizures, severe skin blistering, lactic acidosis.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Level A rescue; strip all clothing/boots immediately. 2. 100% Oxygen. 3. Administer CYANOKIT (Hydroxocobalamin) for systemic toxicity!
chemicals.fire_response: Explosive polymerization in fire! Burns releasing Hydrogen Cyanide (HCN) and NOx.
chemicals.reactivity: Polymerizes explosively with strong bases, acids, amines, or light.
chemicals.storage_temp: Cool dark stabilized tank; ground all lines
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Strong bases, strong acids, bromine, ammonia, copper
chemicals.sds_key_points: Treat Acrylonitrile poisoning as acute Cyanide toxicity + severe chemical burn!

chemicals.name: Alcohols, N.O.S. (Denatured / Industrial Alcohol Blend)
chemicals.symptoms: CNS depression, methanol denaturant risk (blindness/acidosis if ingested).
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Fresh air. 2. Seek ER care if ingested.
chemicals.fire_response: Requires Alcohol-Resistant Foam (AR-AFFF), CO2, or dry chemical.
chemicals.reactivity: Incompatible with oxidizers and nitric acid.
chemicals.storage_temp: Flammable Cabinet
chemicals.sds_key_points: Burns with pale near-invisible flame in bright sun.

chemicals.name: Ammonia Solution (10-35% Aqueous Ammonium Hydroxide)
chemicals.ppe_level: Splash goggles, face shield, butyl/nitrile gloves
chemicals.symptoms: Severe corneal ulceration/blindness, laryngospasm, coughing, caustic esophageal burns.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Immediate 20+ minute eye/skin water irrigation. 2. Humidified oxygen.
chemicals.fire_response: Water fog knocks down ammonia vapors effectively.
chemicals.reactivity: NEVER MIX WITH BLEACH (Sodium Hypochlorite)—produces deadly Chloramine gas!
chemicals.storage_temp: Cool Corrosive Base cabinet
chemicals.sds_key_points: Janitorial and household cleaner. Top pairing in accidental Bleach + Ammonia gas incidents.

chemicals.name: Ammonia, Anhydrous
chemicals.synonyms: Anhydrous ammonia, NH3, Spirit of Hartshorn
chemicals.respirator_req: Level A or Level B with positive-pressure SCBA
chemicals.ppe_level: Level A or Level B (positive pressure SCBA)
chemicals.symptoms: Severe airway/eye caustic burns, laryngospasm, asphyxiation, blindness, coughing, frostbite
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Strip clothing and deluge with water. 2. Airway support (prepare for intubation). 3. 100% oxygen.
chemicals.antidote: No specific chemical antidote. Aggressive irrigation and airway management.
chemicals.fire_response: Water spray knocks down cloud. Confined spaces risk vapor cloud explosion.
chemicals.reactivity: Corrosive to copper, brass. Reacts violently with strong acids, hypochlorite bleach, halogens.
chemicals.storage_temp: Outdoor or well-ventilated bulk tanks with emergency water deluge
chemicals.sds_key_points: Agricultural and industrial refrigeration standard. Highly caustic vapor cloud.

chemicals.name: Ammonium Nitrate (Fertilizer / Technical Grade)
chemicals.respirator_req: SCBA (thermal decomposition releases lethal brown NO2 gas!)
chemicals.symptoms: Dust causes mild irritation; fire decomposition releases dense red-brown Nitrogen Dioxide (NO2) causing fatal delayed pulmonary edema; massive blast overpressure risk!
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Evacuate immediately if fire reaches bulk AN storage! 2. Treat NO2 inhalation with oxygen & 24h observation.
chemicals.fire_response: IF MASSIVE FIRE IMPINGES ON BULK AMMONIUM NITRATE (West, TX / Beirut profile): ABANDON FIREFIGHTING AND EVACUATE 1 MILE (1,600m) IMMEDIATELY! For incipient small fires only, flood with massive open water (never steam or foam, never confine!).
chemicals.reactivity: Contamination with >0.2% fuel oil/diesel (ANFO), sulfur, chlorates, or powdered metals sensitizes AN into a high explosive!
chemicals.storage_temp: Non-combustible concrete floor away from diesel, oil, wood, sulfur, and copper
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Diesel fuel, oils, organic matter, chlorates, acids, powdered metals, confinement in fire
chemicals.sds_key_points: Hard tactical rule: If a bulk Ammonium Nitrate warehouse is on fire, evacuate 1 mile (1600m)—do not fight advanced bulk AN fires!

chemicals.name: Anthrax Spores (Bacillus anthracis - Infectious Substance)
chemicals.respirator_req: Level A/B with SCBA or CBRN PAPR
chemicals.ppe_level: Level B/A with SCBA + Sporicidal Bleach/Peracetic Decon
chemicals.symptoms: Inhalation: flu-like prodrome for 2-4 days, then abrupt hemorrhagic mediastinitis (widened mediastinum on CXR), shock, meningitis, death. Cutaneous: painless black eschar with massive edema.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Wet down envelope/powder gently with sporicidal bleach (10% household bleach / pH-adjusted) or Peracetic Acid (70% alcohol DOES NOT KILL SPORES!). 2. Start Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO BID or Doxycycline 100 mg PO BID x 60 days + Anthrax Vaccine).
chemicals.antidote: Ciprofloxacin or Doxycycline + Raxibacumab / Obiltoxaximab monoclonal antitoxin.
chemicals.fire_response: Avoid disturbing dry powder; isolate HVAC immediately.
chemicals.reactivity: Spores survive alcohol and standard quaternary ammonium disinfectants—require pH-adjusted 0.5-1% Hypochlorite, Chlorine Dioxide, or Peracetic Acid!
chemicals.storage_temp: BSL-3 Select Agent containment
chemicals.sds_key_points: Alcohol and Lysol DO NOT kill Anthrax spores—use sporicidal bleach or peracetic acid + 60-day Ciprofloxacin/Doxycycline!

chemicals.name: Antifreeze / Engine Coolant (Ethylene Glycol)
chemicals.color: Fluorescent bright green, orange, pink, or yellow liquid
chemicals.respirator_req: Organic vapor mask if heated mist generated
chemicals.symptoms: Sweet taste makes it a massive poisoning risk for pets and children. Ingestion leads to severe metabolic acidosis, acute renal failure, calcium oxalate kidney stones, brain damage, coma, and death within 24-72 hours.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Ingestion: Seek emergency hospital treatment IMMEDIATELY. 2. Do not induce vomiting. 3. Wash skin with soap and water.
chemicals.antidote: Fomepizole (Antizol) or IV Ethanol, plus Hemodialysis.
chemicals.fire_response: Combustible liquid at elevated temperatures. Use alcohol-resistant foam, dry chemical, CO2, water fog.
chemicals.reactivity: Incompatible with strong oxidizers, chromium trioxide, potassium permanganate.
chemicals.storage_temp: Ambient temperature, tightly closed original containers
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Strong acids, strong bases, strong oxidizers
chemicals.sds_key_points: High volume retail automotive fluid. Fatal kidney failure if ingested. Treat with Fomepizole.

chemicals.name: Argon, Refrigerated Liquid
chemicals.symptoms: Silent odorless knockdown asphyxiation (1-2 breaths of 100% argon causes immediate loss of consciousness without air-hunger warning!).
chemicals.first_aid: 1. SCBA rescue ONLY (do not become a second victim!). 2. High-flow oxygen & ventilatory support.
chemicals.fire_response: Non-flammable inert gas. Cool tanks with water.
chemicals.reactivity: Inert chemically; physical liquid-to-gas expansion ratio is 1 to 840 (ruptures unvented lines).
chemicals.storage_temp: Well-ventilated area with low-level O2 depletion alarm
chemicals.sds_key_points: 1:840 expansion ratio. Heavy gas (VD 1.38) pools in welding pits and basements.

chemicals.name: Benzene
chemicals.symptoms: Acute: euphoria, dizziness, fatal ventricular arrhythmias ('sniffer's heart'), respiratory arrest. Chronic: Aplastic anemia & Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML).
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Move to fresh air. 2. Strip clothing & wash skin. 3. Avoid epinephrine/adrenaline (triggers V-fib).
chemicals.fire_response: Highly flammable liquid; vapors flash back along ground. Use foam, CO2, dry chemical.
chemicals.reactivity: Explosive reaction with nitric acid, chlorine, ozone, permanganates.
chemicals.storage_temp: Grounded Flammable Cabinet with vapor recovery
chemicals.sds_key_points: Confirmed Group 1 human leukemogen. Freezes into solid crystals at 5.5C (42F)!

chemicals.name: Boron Trifluoride
chemicals.color: Colorless gas (forms dense white HF/boric acid fumes in moist air)
chemicals.symptoms: Severe respiratory burns, fluoride toxicity, corneal opacity, skin necrosis.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Move upwind. 2. Irrigate 15 min + Calcium Gluconate for fluoride burns.
chemicals.fire_response: Reacts with water to form dense toxic fluoroboric/HF mist.
chemicals.reactivity: Explodes with alkali metals and alkyl nitrates.
chemicals.storage_temp: Dry ventilated toxic gas cabinet
chemicals.sds_key_points: Semiconductor & petrochemical catalyst gas.

chemicals.name: Brake Cleaner (Tetrachloroethylene)
chemicals.synonyms: Perchloroethylene, Perc, Non-chlorinated/Chlorinated brake parts cleaner
chemicals.respirator_req: Supplied-air respirator / SCBA (vapor penetrates organic cartridges rapidly)
chemicals.ppe_level: Level B / Viton chemical-resistant gloves (Nitrile is permeated!)
chemicals.symptoms: Dizziness, lightheadedness, headache, sleepiness, cardiac arrhythmia, liver/kidney damage; DANGER: When sprayed on hot exhaust or in welding zone, converts to deadly PHOSGENE GAS!
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Remove to fresh air immediately. 2. Flush skin and eyes with water for 15 min. 3. DO NOT INDUCE VOMITING. 4. Administer oxygen. 5. Avoid epinephrine (sensitizes myocardium).
chemicals.fire_response: Non-flammable liquid, but aerosol cans explode when heated. Produces toxic hydrogen chloride and phosgene gas in fires.
chemicals.reactivity: Decomposes on hot surfaces (>300°C) to phosgene and HCl. Reacts with active metals (aluminum, magnesium).
chemicals.storage_temp: Cool, dry, well-ventilated area (<50°C / 122°F)
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Strong bases, aluminum, zinc, open flames, welding arcs
chemicals.sds_key_points: Common in all auto repair bays. Never use near welding torches. Carcinogen suspect.

chemicals.name: Brake Fluid (DOT 3 / DOT 4 Polyglycol Ether)
chemicals.synonyms: Hydraulic brake fluid, Polyethylene glycol ether + borate esters
chemicals.symptoms: Eye irritation, skin absorption, metabolic acidosis and renal injury if ingested (similar to ethylene glycol).
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Flush eyes 15 min. 2. Wash skin with soap & water. 3. Treat ingestion with Fomepizole/medical evaluation.
chemicals.antidote: Fomepizole if toxic glycol ether ingestion suspected.
chemicals.fire_response: Combustible at high heat; use foam, CO2, dry chemical.
chemicals.reactivity: SPONTANEOUS FIREBALL IF MIXED WITH CALCIUM HYPOCHLORITE (Pool Shock) OR POTASSIUM PERMANGANATE!
chemicals.storage_temp: Tightly sealed container (hygroscopic—absorbs moisture from air) away from oxidizers
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Calcium hypochlorite (Pool Shock), potassium permanganate, strong oxidizers
chemicals.sds_key_points: Classic spontaneous ignition hazard when brake fluid contacts pool chlorine (Calcium Hypochlorite)!

chemicals.name: Calcium Carbide
chemicals.synonyms: Carbide lamp stone, Acetylene generator rock, CaC2
chemicals.hazard_class: 4.3 (Dangerous When Wet - Emits Flammable Acetylene Gas)
chemicals.odor: Garlic-like acetylene odor when exposed to humid air
chemicals.symptoms: Reacts with sweat/tear moisture to form caustic Calcium Hydroxide (lime burns) and explosive Acetylene gas.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Brush off dry powder completely before flushing eyes/skin with large amounts of water.
chemicals.fire_response: DO NOT USE WATER OR FOAM! Smother with dry sand, dry dolomite, or Class D dry powder.
chemicals.reactivity: Contact with water or humid air generates explosive Acetylene gas (C2H2) and heat; explodes with copper/silver salts.
chemicals.storage_temp: Hermetically sealed steel drums in elevated dry room with no sprinklers
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Water, humid air, acids, copper/brass, oxidizers
chemicals.sds_key_points: 1 pound of Calcium Carbide + water generates 4.5 cubic feet of explosive Acetylene gas!

chemicals.name: Calcium Hypochlorite, Dry (Pool Shock)
chemicals.synonyms: HTH Pool Shock, Granular chlorine, Ca(ClO)2
chemicals.respirator_req: Full-face respirator with chlorine cartridge or SCBA
chemicals.symptoms: Severe eye/skin burns, intense coughing and pulmonary edema from chlorine dust/gas.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Brush off dry powder before flooding with water (small amounts of water trigger exothermic chlorine release!). 2. Fresh air + oxygen.
chemicals.fire_response: FLOOD with massive water from a distance—dampening with small amounts of water causes runaway heat and Chlorine gas evolution!
chemicals.reactivity: A single drop of Brake Fluid (Polyglycol), Antifreeze, Soda, or Ammonia onto Pool Shock triggers a violent fireball within 30 seconds!
chemicals.storage_temp: Cool dry oxidizer shelf away from all liquids, oils, and other pool chemicals (Trichlor)
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Brake fluid, ethylene glycol, ammonia, acids, organic trichlor tablets, moisture
chemicals.sds_key_points: Retail hardware & pool store #1 fire starter. Never mix Calcium Hypochlorite with Trichlor tablets or organic fluids!

chemicals.name: Carbon Dioxide, Compressed (Gas Cylinder)
chemicals.synonyms: CO2 cylinder, Beverage carbonation tank, Kegerator gas
chemicals.symptoms: Rapid headache, tachypnea, panic, unconsciousness at >7-10% even when Oxygen is still >18%!
chemicals.first_aid: 1. SCBA rescue from walk-in cooler or basement. 2. 100% Oxygen.
chemicals.fire_response: Cool cylinders in fire.
chemicals.reactivity: Incompatible with active metal dust fires (Mg, Li, Al).
chemicals.storage_temp: Chained upright in ventilated room with CO2 monitor
chemicals.sds_key_points: Walk-in cooler & restaurant soda-fountain leak hazard across all hospitality venues.

chemicals.name: Carbon Dioxide, Refrigerated Liquid
chemicals.synonyms: Liquid CO2, Dry Ice gas, Carbonic anhydride
chemicals.odor: Odorless (stinging sharp bite in nose at >5%)
chemicals.respirator_req: SCBA mandatory (O2 monitors alone do not catch toxic CO2 hypercapnia!)
chemicals.symptoms: At 4-5%: air hunger, panic, bounding pulse, headache; at 10%: unconsciousness in <1 min; dry ice contact (-78.5C) causes severe frostbite.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. SCBA rescue from basement/cellar. 2. 100% Oxygen. 3. Warm frostbite.
chemicals.fire_response: Non-flammable extinguishment gas. Beware static electricity discharge when venting CO2 near flammable vapors!
chemicals.reactivity: Dust explosions of Mg, Al, Ti, and Li burn MORE violently inside CO2 (strips oxygen from CO2)!
chemicals.storage_temp: Ventilated beverage/brewery room with CO2 alarm set at 5,000 ppm & 30,000 ppm
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Active metal fires (Mg, Li, Na, Al dust), alkali bases
chemicals.sds_key_points: Every restaurant, brewery, and fast-food CO2 bulk tank in Pueblo/Colorado Springs carries basement asphyxiation risk!

chemicals.name: Carbon Monoxide, Compressed
chemicals.odor: Completely odorless and tasteless (The Silent Killer)
chemicals.respirator_req: Positive-pressure SCBA strictly required (APR cartridges DO NOT filter CO!)
chemicals.symptoms: Throbbing headache, nausea, confusion, syncope, seizures, cardiac ischemia, coma, death. Pulse oximeter (SpO2) gives FALSE NORMAL reading (use CO-oximeter)!
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Immediate rescue with SCBA. 2. 100% Non-Rebreather mask oxygen or Hyperbaric Oxygen (HBO) for carboxyhemoglobin >25% or neuro/pregnant patients.
chemicals.antidote: 100% High-Flow Normobaric or Hyperbaric Oxygen (reduces COHb half-life from 300 min to 20-80 min).
chemicals.fire_response: Flammable gas (LEL 12.5% to UEL 74%). Cool cylinders from cover.
chemicals.reactivity: Reacts with interhalogens, oxidizers.
chemicals.storage_temp: Ventilated cylinder locker with CO sensor
chemicals.sds_key_points: Standard SpO2 finger probes cannot distinguish carboxyhemoglobin from oxyhemoglobin!

chemicals.name: Carburetor & Throttle Body Cleaner
chemicals.odor: Strong sweet pungent ketone / aromatic solvent odor
chemicals.respirator_req: Organic vapor cartridge with particulate pre-filter
chemicals.ppe_level: Safety goggles, butyl or nitrile gloves
chemicals.symptoms: Immediate eye stinging, dizziness, headache, nausea, respiratory irritation, defatting of skin, CNS depression
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Move to fresh air. 2. Flush eyes with water for 15 minutes. 3. Wash skin with soap and water. 4. If swallowed, do NOT induce vomiting.
chemicals.fire_response: Extremely flammable! Cans rocket and explode in fires. Use CO2, dry chemical, or water fog from protected position.
chemicals.reactivity: Vapors are heavier than air and accumulate in service pits. Incompatible with strong oxidizers.
chemicals.storage_temp: Below 50°C (122°F). Do not store in direct sunlight or hot vehicles.
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Oxidizing agents, heat, sparks, open flames
chemicals.sds_key_points: Universal automotive cleaner sold in all auto stores. Major rocket projectile hazard in garage fires.

chemicals.name: Chlorine
chemicals.ppe_level: Level A (Gas-tight, fully encapsulating suit + SCBA)
chemicals.symptoms: Severe eye and nose burning, coughing, choking, delayed pulmonary edema, frothy pink sputum, skin burns
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Remove upwind immediately. 2. Absolute bed rest. 3. 100% humidified oxygen. 4. 15-min eye/skin flush. 5. Strip clothing.
chemicals.antidote: Supportive therapy; nebulized beta-agonists and systemic corticosteroids.
chemicals.fire_response: Do NOT apply water into spill (forms hydrochloric acid). Use water spray upwind to absorb gas.
chemicals.reactivity: Violent oxidizer. Reacts explosively with hydrocarbons, ammonia, hydrogen.
chemicals.storage_temp: Dedicated ventilated gas cylinder room, chained upright
chemicals.sds_key_points: High industrial rail transit. Water spray must not hit liquid leak.

chemicals.name: Chloroform (Trichloromethane)
chemicals.symptoms: Rapid CNS anesthesia, respiratory depression, fatal cardiac arrhythmia (myocardial sensitization to catecholamines), hepatorenal necrosis.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Fresh air + oxygen. 2. Avoid epinephrine! 3. Wash skin.
chemicals.antidote: N-acetylcysteine may reduce hepatotoxicity; supportive care.
chemicals.fire_response: Non-flammable, but decomposes in fire or sunlight/air to deadly PHOSGENE GAS (COCl2)!
chemicals.reactivity: Explodes when mixed with Acetone + Base (NaOH/KOH) or Alkali Metals!
chemicals.storage_temp: Dark amber bottle in ventilated poison cabinet
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Acetone + bases, sodium, potassium, aluminum, strong alkalis
chemicals.sds_key_points: Never mix Chloroform and Acetone in the presence of any base—triggers violent exothermic lab explosion!

chemicals.name: Dichloromethane (Methylene Chloride / Paint Stripper)
chemicals.synonyms: Methylene chloride, DCM, Aircraft paint stripper
chemicals.respirator_req: Supplied-Air Respirator / SCBA ONLY (breaks through organic cartridges in minutes!)
chemicals.ppe_level: PVA or Silver-Shield gloves (destroys Nitrile and Latex!) + SCBA
chemicals.symptoms: Rapid narcosis/unconsciousness in enclosed rooms/bathtubs, plus LIVER METABOLISM CONVERTS DCM INTO CARBON MONOXIDE (COHb continues rising for hours after removal from scene!)!
chemicals.first_aid: 1. SCBA rescue. 2. 100% High-Flow Oxygen (monitor Carboxyhemoglobin COHb for 12-24 hours!). 3. Strip contaminated clothes.
chemicals.antidote: 100% Normobaric or Hyperbaric Oxygen for endogenous Carbon Monoxide poisoning.
chemicals.fire_response: Forms flammable vapor-air mixtures at >100C and decomposes in flames to Phosgene and HCl.
chemicals.reactivity: Reacts violently with alkali metals, aluminum powder, nitric acid, and strong oxidizers.
chemicals.storage_temp: Cool ventilated toxic cabinet
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Alkali metals, aluminum, nitric acid, open flames (forms Phosgene!)
chemicals.sds_key_points: Unique clinical pearl: Methylene Chloride is metabolized by the liver into Carbon Monoxide—CO levels keep climbing after rescue!

chemicals.name: Diesel Exhaust Fluid (DEF / Aqueous Urea 32.5%)
chemicals.odor: Slight faint ammonia odor when heated
chemicals.symptoms: Mild eye and skin irritation; crystallizes into white urea crust when dried. If heated in fire (>130C), decomposes into Ammonia (NH3) and Biuret.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Flush eyes/skin with water. 2. Rinse spills with water.
chemicals.fire_response: Non-flammable water-based solution; cools fires, though intense fire decomposes urea to Ammonia vapor.
chemicals.reactivity: NEVER mix DEF with Sodium Hypochlorite (Bleach) or Calcium Hypochlorite—urea + hypochlorite reacts to form explosive Nitrogen Trichloride (NCl3) and Chloramines!
chemicals.storage_temp: Store between -5C and 30C in HDPE or stainless steel (corrodes copper, brass, and carbon steel!)
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Hypochlorite bleach, nitrites, strong oxidizers, copper/brass
chemicals.sds_key_points: Stocked in every truck stop and shop. Non-hazardous alone, but reacts violently if mixed with Bleach/Pool Shock!

chemicals.name: Diesel Fuel / No. 2 Heating Oil
chemicals.synonyms: Fuel Oil #2, Red-dyed off-road diesel, Ultra-low sulfur diesel (ULSD)
chemicals.color: Clear, straw-yellow, or red-dyed oily liquid
chemicals.ppe_level: Nitrile gloves, splash goggles, oil-resistant boots
chemicals.symptoms: Skin defatting/dermatitis, chemical pneumonitis on aspiration, high-pressure fuel-injector puncture causes gangrenous tissue necrosis.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. High-pressure injection injury requires immediate surgical decompression! 2. Do not induce vomiting. 3. Wash skin with soap.
chemicals.fire_response: Foam, dry chemical, CO2, or water fog. Cool exposed fuel tanks with water spray.
chemicals.reactivity: Forms explosive ANFO mixture when mixed with Ammonium Nitrate fertilizer.
chemicals.storage_temp: Bunded fuel tank or flammable cabinet away from Ammonium Nitrate
chemicals.sds_key_points: Saddle-tank ruptures occur on every tractor-trailer crash. Never store near Ammonium Nitrate.

chemicals.name: Dimethylamine, Anhydrous
chemicals.symptoms: Severe corneal edema ('blue haze' vision), caustic airway burns, flash fire.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Flush eyes/skin 15 min. 2. Humidified oxygen.
chemicals.fire_response: Alcohol-resistant foam, water spray, dry chemical.
chemicals.reactivity: Explodes with mercury; reacts violently with acids and oxidizers.
chemicals.storage_temp: Cool ventilated cylinder bay
chemicals.sds_key_points: Distinctive rotting-fish odor.

chemicals.name: Epichlorohydrin
chemicals.symptoms: Delayed severe deep skin blistering, pulmonary edema, kidney/liver necrosis, male sterility, human carcinogen.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Strip clothing & wash skin 20 min. 2. Observe 24h for pulmonary edema.
chemicals.fire_response: Runaway polymerization hazard in fire; releases HCl and Phosgene.
chemicals.reactivity: Explosive polymerization with acids, bases, amines, ferric chloride, or zinc.
chemicals.storage_temp: Cool ventilated poison/flammable vault
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Acids, bases, amines, aluminum, zinc, iron salts
chemicals.sds_key_points: Primary building block of two-part epoxy resins and coatings.

chemicals.name: Ethanol (Ethyl Alcohol / Denatured Alcohol / E85-E98)
chemicals.synonyms: Grain alcohol, Fuel ethanol, Denatured spirits
chemicals.ppe_level: Turnout gear + SCBA or nitrile gloves
chemicals.symptoms: Eye irritation, CNS intoxication, hypoglycemia.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Fresh air. 2. Flush eyes.
chemicals.fire_response: CRITICAL FIRE RULE: Standard hydrocarbon AFFF foam is immediately dissolved by Ethanol! You MUST use Alcohol-Resistant Foam (AR-AFFF) at 0.15-0.20 gpm/sq ft!
chemicals.reactivity: Reacts violently with nitric acid, hydrogen peroxide, perchlorates, permanganates.
chemicals.storage_temp: Grounded Flammable Cabinet / bulk tank
chemicals.sds_key_points: Unit-train rail tank car cargo across Colorado. Requires Alcohol-Resistant Foam (AR-AFFF)—standard foam fails!

chemicals.name: Ethylene Oxide
chemicals.odor: Sweet ether-like odor at high toxic levels (>500 ppm)
chemicals.symptoms: Severe eye/skin blisters, vomiting, neuropathy, pulmonary edema, potent human carcinogen & mutagen.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Strip clothing immediately (leather/rubber absorbs EtO!). 2. Flush 15 min. 3. Oxygen.
chemicals.fire_response: EXTREME BLEVE / RUNAWAY POLYMERIZATION HAZARD! Burns even in the absence of air (100% UEL). Evacuate 1 mile (1600m) if tank involved in fire.
chemicals.reactivity: Contamination with trace acid, base, ammonia, or rust triggers violent runaway polymerization.
chemicals.storage_temp: Dedicated refrigerated sterilizer vault with water deluge
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Acids, bases, rust/iron oxide, copper, ammonia
chemicals.sds_key_points: Used in medical device sterilization plants along the Front Range. 100% Upper Explosive Limit.

chemicals.name: Fentanyl / Carfentanil (Illicit Synthetic Opioid Powder)
chemicals.physical_state: Solid crystalline powder / pressed tablets / liquid aerosol
chemicals.color: White, tan, or blue pressed powder
chemicals.respirator_req: P100 / N100 APR or PAPR/SCBA if powder is airborne/milled
chemicals.ppe_level: Double Nitrile gloves (min 5 mil) + N95/P100 + goggles (Level A if bulk aerosolized)
chemicals.symptoms: OPIOID OVERDOSE TRIAD: Pinpoint pupils (miosis), profound CNS coma, and rapid respiratory arrest (apnea) + wooden-chest wall rigidity! Note: Intact dry skin absorption is extremely slow, but inhalation or mucosal/eye contact is rapidly fatal.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Ventilate & support breathing with Bag-Valve-Mask (BVM) immediately! 2. Administer NALOXONE (Narcan 2-4 mg IN/IM/IV; repeat every 2-3 min up to 10-20 mg for Carfentanil!). 3. Wash skin with SOAP AND WATER ONLY—NEVER USE ALCOHOL HAND SANITIZER (alcohol accelerates skin absorption 10x!).
chemicals.antidote: Naloxone HCl (Narcan 2-4 mg IN/IV repeated q2-3m; high doses required for Carfentanil).
chemicals.fire_response: Do not use high-pressure water jets that loft dry powder into air; wet down gently with soap spray.
chemicals.reactivity: Destroyed/deactivated by Peracetic Acid, Oxone, or Household Bleach + Soap (verify pH). Never use alcohol sanitizer on skin!
chemicals.storage_temp: Evidence lockbox
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Alcohol hand sanitizers on skin (increases dermal flux!), aerosolization
chemicals.sds_key_points: CRITICAL FIELD RULE: Never use alcohol hand sanitizer after touching suspected Fentanyl—wash with soap and water!

chemicals.name: Ferric Chloride, Solution
chemicals.synonyms: Iron(III) chloride, Wastewater coagulant, PCB etchant
chemicals.symptoms: Corrosive eye damage, skin burns, stains skin yellow-brown.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Flush eyes/skin 15 min with water.
chemicals.fire_response: Attacks metals (aluminum, steel, copper) to evolve flammable Hydrogen gas.
chemicals.reactivity: Catalyzes violent runaway polymerization of Ethylene Oxide and Styrene!
chemicals.storage_temp: Fiberglass or HDPE tank
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Metals, strong bases, ethylene oxide, styrene, sodium
chemicals.sds_key_points: Bulk water-treatment chemical across Front Range utilities.

chemicals.name: Flammable Liquid, Corrosive, N.O.S. (Amine / Methoxide Solutions)
chemicals.synonyms: Sodium methoxide in methanol, Biodiesel catalyst
chemicals.symptoms: Dual hazard: severe caustic liquefactive burns + methanol systemic toxicity + flash fire!
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Deluge skin/eyes 30 min. 2. Treat for methanol toxicity (Fomepizole).
chemicals.fire_response: Alcohol-resistant foam or dry chemical (water reacts exothermically with concentrated methoxide!).
chemicals.reactivity: Reacts violently with water, acids, and oxidizers.
chemicals.storage_temp: Dry grounded flammable/corrosive cabinet
chemicals.sds_key_points: Used in biodiesel production and chemical synthesis.

chemicals.name: Formaldehyde, Solution (Formalin 37%)
chemicals.symptoms: Intense lacrimation, coughing, bronchospasm, laryngeal edema, severe allergic contact dermatitis, nasopharyngeal carcinogen.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Fresh air + humidified oxygen. 2. Flush eyes/skin 15 min. 3. Milk/water dilution if swallowed.
chemicals.antidote: Fomepizole or Sodium Bicarbonate IV for severe metabolic acidosis (formic acid conversion).
chemicals.fire_response: Alcohol-resistant foam, water spray, dry chemical.
chemicals.reactivity: Reacts with Hydrochloric Acid (HCl) or Hypochlorites in moist air to form Bis(chloromethyl) ether (potent lung carcinogen!).
chemicals.storage_temp: Ventilated cabinet at 15-25C (cold causes paraformaldehyde precipitation)
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Hydrochloric acid, bleach, oxidizers, strong alkalis
chemicals.sds_key_points: Never allow Formaldehyde and Hydrochloric Acid vapors to mix—forms lethal Bis(chloromethyl) ether!

chemicals.name: Fuel, Aviation, Turbine Engine (Jet A / JP-8)
chemicals.synonyms: Jet A, Jet A-1, JP-8, Kerosene aviation fuel
chemicals.respirator_req: Organic vapor + P100 respirator or SCBA
chemicals.ppe_level: Turnout gear + SCBA or nitrile gloves
chemicals.symptoms: Aspiration pneumonitis, CNS dizziness, dermatitis.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Fresh air. 2. Do NOT induce vomiting.
chemicals.fire_response: AFFF / Fluoroprotein foam, dry chemical, CO2. High static accumulator during fueling.
chemicals.reactivity: Incompatible with strong oxidizers.
chemicals.storage_temp: Grounded fuel tank
chemicals.sds_key_points: Airport & military convoy tanker fuel (Pueblo Memorial Airport / Fort Carson corridor).

chemicals.name: Gasoline (Motor Fuel / Petrol)
chemicals.color: Clear, amber, or dyed pink/red liquid
chemicals.ppe_level: Turnout gear + SCBA or Viton/nitrile splash protection
chemicals.symptoms: Headache, vertigo, ataxia, chemical pneumonitis if aspirated, thermal burns from flash fire, benzene hematologic toxicity.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Fresh air. 2. Wash skin with soap & water. 3. NEVER induce vomiting (fatal aspiration pneumonitis risk).
chemicals.fire_response: Use Class B AFFF / alcohol-resistant foam (for E10-E85 blends), dry chemical, or CO2. Water stream spreads burning fuel on surface!
chemicals.reactivity: Explosive vapor-air mixtures down to -43C. Reacts violently with nitric acid, hydrogen peroxide, halogens.
chemicals.storage_temp: UL-listed Flammable Cabinet or underground tank
chemicals.sds_key_points: Most common highway cargo tank rollover spill (DOT-406). Dike storm drains immediately.

chemicals.name: Household & Commercial Bleach (Sodium Hypochlorite)
chemicals.synonyms: Liquid bleach, Chlorox, Soda bleach lye, NaOCl 6-12%
chemicals.color: Clear pale yellow to green liquid
chemicals.osha_pel: None established for solution (Chlorine gas PEL: 1 ppm Ceiling)
chemicals.respirator_req: Half-mask with acid gas / chlorine cartridge
chemicals.symptoms: Severe eye stinging and corneal damage, skin irritation/burns, coughing and airway irritation. CRITICAL WARNING: Mixing bleach with Ammonia creates toxic CHLORAMINE GAS; mixing bleach with Acid creates deadly CHLORINE GAS!
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Flush skin and eyes with water for 15+ minutes. 2. Inhalation: Move to fresh air immediately. 3. Ingestion: Drink 1-2 glasses of water or milk to dilute. Do NOT induce vomiting.
chemicals.fire_response: Non-combustible liquid, but decomposes on heating to release chlorine and oxygen, feeding fires. Use water spray to keep drums cool.
chemicals.reactivity: NEVER MIX WITH AMMONIA (forms chloramine gas) OR ACIDS (forms chlorine gas). Reacts violently with organic solvents.
chemicals.storage_temp: Cool (<25°C), dark, ventilated area (heat and sunlight degrade bleach rapidly)
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Acids, Ammonia, organic solvents, peroxides, reducing agents
chemicals.sds_key_points: #1 cause of consumer hazmat toxic gas generation when mixed with toilet bowl cleaner or ammonia. High retail volume (Walmart, Amazon).

chemicals.name: Hydrochloric Acid (Muriatic Acid)
chemicals.synonyms: Muriatic acid, Pool acid, Aqueous Hydrogen Chloride
chemicals.respirator_req: Acid gas cartridge + P100 or SCBA
chemicals.ppe_level: Acid splash goggles, face shield, neoprene/nitrile gloves
chemicals.symptoms: Severe corneal burns, skin ulceration, laryngeal spasm, choking, dental enamel erosion.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Flush eyes/skin 20+ minutes. 2. Humidified oxygen + nebulized bronchodilators for vapor inhalation.
chemicals.antidote: Supportive care; soda ash / lime for spill neutralization.
chemicals.fire_response: Non-flammable, but attacks metals (zinc, galvanized steel, aluminum) to liberate explosive H2 gas.
chemicals.reactivity: Mixing with Bleach (Sodium Hypochlorite) instantly releases deadly CHLORINE GAS! Reacts violently with bases.
chemicals.storage_temp: Blue polyethylene acid cabinet (never metal shelves—fumes rust steel rapidly)
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Bleach/hypochlorites, bases, cyanides, sulfides, active metals
chemicals.sds_key_points: Sold in gallon jugs at Home Depot/Lowe's for concrete etching and pool pH.

chemicals.name: Hydrofluoric Acid, Solution (Wheel & Aluminum Brightener)
chemicals.synonyms: Aqueous HF, Mag wheel cleaner, Glass etching acid
chemicals.symptoms: Dilute solutions (<20%) cause NO immediate pain for up to 12 hours, then cause excruciating deep bone pain, tissue liquefaction, and fatal cardiac arrest from hypocalcemia!
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Rinse 5 min, then massage 2.5% CALCIUM GLUCONATE GEL into burn site continuously! 2. Immediate ER cardiac monitoring + serum Ca/Mg/K.
chemicals.antidote: 2.5% Calcium Gluconate Gel (topical) + IV/Intra-arterial Calcium Gluconate.
chemicals.fire_response: Attacks glass, concrete, and metals (producing H2).
chemicals.reactivity: Dissolves glass/quartz; reacts with bases and metals.
chemicals.storage_temp: Polyethylene bottle inside locked poison/acid cabinet
chemicals.sds_key_points: Hidden killer in commercial truck-wash / aluminum wheel brighteners. Always stock 2.5% Calcium Gluconate gel!

chemicals.name: Hydrogen Cyanide, Stabilized
chemicals.synonyms: Hydrocyanic acid, Prussic acid, AC Blood Agent, HCN
chemicals.odor: Bitter almonds (40% of people genetically cannot smell it!)
chemicals.respirator_req: Level A CBRN Suit + SCBA (rapidly absorbed through intact skin!)
chemicals.symptoms: Rapid gasping tachypnea, cherry-red venous blood, lactic acidosis (>8 mmol/L), seizures, apnea, cardiac arrest within 1-3 minutes.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Level A rescue. 2. 100% Oxygen. 3. Administer CYANOKIT (Hydroxocobalamin 5g IV over 15 min) or Sodium Thiosulfate immediately!
chemicals.antidote: Hydroxocobalamin (Cyanokit 5g IV) or Nithiodote (Sodium Nitrite + Sodium Thiosulfate).
chemicals.fire_response: Extremely flammable and prone to explosive polymerization if unstabilized. Fight from maximum distance.
chemicals.reactivity: Polymerizes explosively with bases/amines/ammonia. Generated when any Cyanide salt contacts Acid.
chemicals.storage_temp: Refrigerated, acid-stabilized cylinder in toxic vault
chemicals.sds_key_points: Key combustion toxin in structure fires (burning polyurethane foam/nylon) and industrial plating hazard.

chemicals.name: Hydrogen Fluoride, Anhydrous
chemicals.ppe_level: Level A Suit + SCBA (etching destroys glass facepieces—use polycarbonate/Mylar cover!)
chemicals.symptoms: Deep penetrating fluoride ion tissue destruction, excruciating pain out of proportion to visible burn, fatal HYPOCALCEMIA & HYPERKALEMIA causing ventricular fibrillation!
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Irrigate immediately. 2. Apply 2.5% CALCIUM GLUCONATE GEL continuously with gloved hand. 3. Nebulized 2.5% Calcium Gluconate for inhalation. 4. Continuous ECG + IV Calcium Gluconate.
chemicals.antidote: Calcium Gluconate (Topical 2.5% gel, Nebulized 2.5%, Intra-arterial / IV infusion). NEVER use Calcium Chloride subcutaneously!
chemicals.fire_response: Reacts violently with water releasing heat and toxic mist. Knock down vapor cloud from upwind with fog.
chemicals.reactivity: Dissolves glass, concrete, silica (forming toxic SiF4), and attacks metals to generate explosive H2.
chemicals.storage_temp: Monel or Teflon-lined steel cylinder; NEVER glass
chemicals.sds_key_points: Even a 2% body surface area burn with concentrated HF can cause fatal cardiac arrest from hypocalcemia!

chemicals.name: Hydrogen Peroxide, Concentrated (>60%)
chemicals.ppe_level: Level B Viton/PVC suit + SCBA (NEVER wear leather or cotton—spontaneous ignition!)
chemicals.symptoms: White bleaching skin burns (emphysema blisters), corneal ulceration, cerebral gas embolism if ingested!
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Flood with water 15+ min. 2. Soak contaminated clothing immediately in water to prevent spontaneous ignition!
chemicals.antidote: Supportive care; hyperbaric oxygen if portal/cerebral gas embolism occurs.
chemicals.fire_response: Decomposes rapidly releasing massive Oxygen + heat. Contamination of drum causes catastrophic overpressure rupture.
chemicals.reactivity: Rust, iron, copper, brass, acetone, or alcohols trigger explosive decomposition (forms TATP with acetone + acid!).
chemicals.storage_temp: Vented passivated aluminum or polyethylene drum in cool oxidizer room
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Organic solvents (acetone, alcohols), transition metals (rust, copper), combustibles
chemicals.sds_key_points: Never return poured H2O2 back into original container—trace dust/rust causes drum explosion!

chemicals.name: Hydrogen Sulfide
chemicals.odor: Rotten eggs (<1 ppm). Olfactory fatigue paralyzes smell above 100 ppm!
chemicals.ppe_level: Level A or Level B with positive-pressure SCBA
chemicals.symptoms: Instant knockdown, collapse, respiratory paralysis, sudden death
chemicals.first_aid: 1. SCBA rescue only. 2. 100% high flow oxygen. 3. CPR/defibrillation if needed.
chemicals.antidote: Amyl Nitrite / Sodium Nitrite IV. Hyperbaric oxygen.
chemicals.fire_response: Extremely flammable. Burns to toxic sulfur dioxide (SO2).
chemicals.reactivity: Explodes with strong oxidizers, nitric acid.
chemicals.storage_temp: Well-ventilated gas cylinder room
chemicals.sds_key_points: Oil & gas, sewer entry hazard. Deadliest confined space gas.

chemicals.name: Hydrogen, Compressed
chemicals.ppe_level: Turnout gear + SCBA + Thermal Imaging Camera (TIC)
chemicals.symptoms: Burns with a nearly INVISIBLE PALE FLAME in daylight and emits almost zero radiant heat until you walk into the flame! Asphyxiation in overhead ceiling pockets.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Treat thermal burns. 2. Administer oxygen.
chemicals.fire_response: USE THERMAL IMAGING CAMERA (TIC) OR BROOM WORKFLOW TO DETECT INVISIBLE FLAME! Wide flammable range (4% to 75% in air) and tiny ignition energy (0.017 mJ).
chemicals.reactivity: Explodes on contact with chlorine in sunlight, fluorine, or oxidizers.
chemicals.storage_temp: Outdoor roof-vented rack (gas rises at 20 m/s)
chemicals.sds_key_points: Lightest gas known (VD 0.07). Always use Thermal Imaging Camera to spot invisible hydrogen jet fires.

chemicals.name: Isopropyl Alcohol (Isopropanol / Rubbing Alcohol)
chemicals.symptoms: Drowsiness, ataxia, gastritis, hemorrhagic tracheobronchitis, ketosis (converts to acetone in liver without severe acidosis).
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Fresh air. 2. Flush eyes. 3. Supportive care if ingested.
chemicals.antidote: Supportive care (do NOT administer Fomepizole—IPA metabolizes to acetone, not toxic acid).
chemicals.fire_response: Alcohol-resistant foam (AR-AFFF), CO2, dry chemical, or water spray dilution.
chemicals.reactivity: Old anhydrous IPA containers exposed to light/air can form shock-sensitive diisopropyl ether peroxides around the cap threads!
chemicals.storage_temp: Flammable Cabinet
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Strong oxidizers, phosgene, aluminum at high temp
chemicals.sds_key_points: High-volume hospital, electronics, and retail warehouse flammable liquid.

chemicals.name: Lead-Acid Automotive Battery Electrolyte (Battery Acid)
chemicals.synonyms: Car battery acid, Sulfuric acid 35-40%, Auto battery
chemicals.odor: Odorless cold; sharp acrid choking odor if overheated
chemicals.respirator_req: Half-mask with acid gas cartridge + P100 filter
chemicals.ppe_level: Level C/B: Rubber splash apron, face shield, heavy neoprene gloves
chemicals.symptoms: Instant severe chemical burns to skin, permanent eye damage/blindness, tooth erosion, respiratory burns if mist inhaled. Charging generates explosive hydrogen gas!
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Flood skin and eyes with continuous water stream for 20+ minutes. 2. Remove contaminated clothes under water. 3. Do not induce vomiting if ingested; give milk or water.
chemicals.antidote: Copious water irrigation; supportive burn management.
chemicals.fire_response: Use CO2, dry chemical, or water spray. Do NOT spray water into cracked hot battery cells. Charging batteries generate explosive hydrogen gas (H2)—eliminate all spark/flame sources.
chemicals.reactivity: Reacts violently with alkalis (baking soda / lime neutralizes safely with foaming). Attacks steel, copper, releasing hydrogen.
chemicals.storage_temp: Well-ventilated battery charging area, ambient temp
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Bases, organic solvents, metal shavings, open sparks
chemicals.sds_key_points: Stocked at every AutoZone, Walmart Auto, O'Reilly. Neutralize spills with sodium bicarbonate. Keep fire extinguisher nearby.

chemicals.name: Lithium-Ion Batteries (Consumer & EV)
chemicals.synonyms: Li-ion cell, Power tool battery, Laptop battery, EV battery pack, LiCoO2
chemicals.odor: Sweet organic solvent / nail polish odor prior to thermal runaway venting
chemicals.respirator_req: SCBA strictly mandatory during battery fires (emits deadly HF gas)
chemicals.symptoms: Smoke inhalation from burning packs causes severe pulmonary damage and fluoride toxicity due to HYDROFLUORIC ACID (HF) and carbon monoxide emission.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Remove from toxic smoke plume immediately. 2. High-flow oxygen. 3. If exposed to smoke, treat for potential HF inhalation (nebulized 2.5% calcium gluconate).
chemicals.antidote: Calcium Gluconate for Hydrofluoric acid exposure.
chemicals.fire_response: THERMAL RUNAWAY IS SELF-SUSTAINING (cells produce their own oxygen). Apply massive continuous water flow (thousands of gallons) directly to the battery enclosure to cool adjacent cells. Do not use dry chemical for extinguishment (cannot cool below critical runaway temp).
chemicals.reactivity: Mechanical crush, puncture, overcharge, or exposure to heat (>60°C) triggers uncontrollable thermal runaway, explosion, and toxic gas release.
chemicals.storage_temp: 15°C to 25°C (59°F to 77°F); State of charge 30-50% for long-term storage
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: High temperatures (>50°C), metal racks causing short circuits, combustible packing pallets, moisture
chemicals.sds_key_points: Massive warehouse hazard (Amazon fulfillment, Walmart logistics). Damaged or swollen batteries must be isolated in pyro-sand drums.

chemicals.name: Methane, Refrigerated Liquid (LNG)
chemicals.color: Colorless liquid; dense white cold vapor cloud
chemicals.odor: Odorless (LNG is NOT odorized with mercaptan!)
chemicals.symptoms: Severe deep cryogenic tissue freezing (-161C), silent asphyxiation (odorless), massive vapor cloud flash fire.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. SCBA rescue. 2. Thaw cryogenic burns in 40C warm water. 3. High-flow oxygen.
chemicals.fire_response: Do NOT apply water directly into cryogenic LNG pool (causes Rapid Phase Transition explosion and accelerates vaporization)! Use high-expansion foam.
chemicals.reactivity: Violent reaction with liquid oxygen, chlorine trifluoride, halogens.
chemicals.storage_temp: ASME cryogenic vacuum-jacketed tank
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Oxidizers, halogens, water stream in pool
chemicals.sds_key_points: Cold LNG vapor is heavier than air until warmed, then rises. Odorless hazard.

chemicals.name: Methyl Bromide (Bromomethane)
chemicals.odor: Odorless at toxic levels (sweetish chloroform odor only at >1000 ppm)
chemicals.respirator_req: SCBA mandatory (penetrates all organic cartridges and rubber!)
chemicals.symptoms: 4 to 48h delayed onset of intractable seizures, myoclonus, pulmonary edema, renal failure, and severe chemical blisters under boots/gloves!
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Strip all clothing & leather boots immediately (traps gas against skin!). 2. Observe 48h for delayed seizures/edema.
chemicals.fire_response: Forms explosive mixtures at high ignition energy; reacts with aluminum to form pyrophoric methylaluminum!
chemicals.reactivity: Never use aluminum fittings or pipes with Methyl Bromide!
chemicals.storage_temp: Locked ventilated fumigant cylinder bay
chemicals.sds_key_points: Agricultural & quarantine fumigant. Penetrates rubber and leather boots!

chemicals.name: Methyl Ethyl Ketone (MEK / 2-Butanone)
chemicals.synonyms: Butanone, MEK, PVC pipe primer solvent
chemicals.symptoms: Severe eye/nose irritation, headache, numbness in extremities (potentiates peripheral neuropathies!).
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Fresh air. 2. Flush eyes 15 min.
chemicals.fire_response: Alcohol-resistant foam, dry chemical, CO2.
chemicals.reactivity: Forms explosive peroxides with hydrogen peroxide/nitric acid; ignites with potassium tert-butoxide.
chemicals.storage_temp: Grounded Flammable Cabinet
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Oxidizers, peroxides, strong bases, chlorosulfonic acid
chemicals.sds_key_points: Plumbing PVC primer and industrial coating solvent. Note: MEK Peroxide (UN3105) is a separate high-hazard organic peroxide!

chemicals.name: Methyl Ethyl Ketone Peroxide (MEKP - Fiberglass Hardener)
chemicals.symptoms: EXTREME CORNEAL BLINDNESS RISK: Even a single tiny splash drop causes irreversible corneal destruction and blindness unless irrigated within seconds! Severe esophageal burns.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. IRRIGATE EYES IMMEDIATELY FOR 30+ MINUTES (Delayed irrigation >30 seconds often results in permanent blindness!). 2. Wash skin with soap & water.
chemicals.antidote: Immediate continuous eye irrigation + Vitamin C (ascorbate) ophthalmic drops per toxicologist.
chemicals.fire_response: Self-Accelerating Decomposition Temperature (SADT ~60C)! Once burning, provides its own oxygen and explodes if confined. Fight from cover with water deluge.
chemicals.reactivity: Contamination with Cobalt Naphthenate promoter, rust, iron, copper, or acetone causes instant explosion!
chemicals.storage_temp: Cool (<25C) dedicated Organic Peroxide locker in original vented plastic bottle ONLY
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Cobalt promoters, accelerators, rust/metals, acetone, strong acids/bases
chemicals.sds_key_points: Auto body & boat fiberglass resin hardener. Never mix MEKP directly with Cobalt Promoter—instant detonation!

chemicals.name: Nitric Acid, Red Fuming (RFNA)
chemicals.synonyms: Aqua fortis, Fuming nitric acid, HNO3
chemicals.respirator_req: Level A or Level B + SCBA
chemicals.symptoms: Turns skin bright yellow (xanthoproteic reaction) with deep necrotic burns; inhalation of red-brown NO2 fumes causes lethal delayed pulmonary edema 6-24h later!
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Deluge skin/eyes 20+ min. 2. Mandatory 24-hour ICU observation for delayed lung edema. 3. 100% Oxygen.
chemicals.antidote: Corticosteroids & PEEP for delayed pulmonary edema; Methylene blue if methemoglobinemia develops.
chemicals.fire_response: Powerful oxidizer—spontaneously ignites wood, sawdust, turpentine, and organic rags!
chemicals.reactivity: Explosive reaction with acetone, alcohols, aniline, turpentine, ammonia, hydrogen sulfide.
chemicals.storage_temp: Dedicated compartmentalized nitric acid cabinet (isolate from acetic/organic acids!)
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Organic solvents, wood/paper/sawdust, bases, cyanides, metals
chemicals.sds_key_points: Never absorb Nitric Acid spills with sawdust, paper, or organic rags—they will burst into flame! Use dry sand or vermiculite.

chemicals.name: Nitrobenzene
chemicals.color: Pale yellow to brown oily liquid
chemicals.symptoms: PROFOUND METHEMOGLOBINEMIA: Turns patient's lips and skin slate-gray/blue ('chocolate-brown arterial blood'), headache, coma, hemolysis. Absorbs rapidly through shoes and clothing!
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Strip clothing & scrub skin with soap/water. 2. 100% Oxygen. 3. Administer METHYLENE BLUE (1-2 mg/kg IV over 5 min)!
chemicals.antidote: Methylene Blue (1-2 mg/kg IV of 1% solution).
chemicals.fire_response: Foam, dry chemical, CO2. Releases toxic NOx in fire.
chemicals.reactivity: Explosive mixtures with nitric acid, potassium hydroxide, or aluminum chloride.
chemicals.storage_temp: Locked poison cabinet
chemicals.sds_key_points: Classic trigger of Methemoglobinemia (chocolate-brown blood + SpO2 stuck at ~85%) treated with IV Methylene Blue!

chemicals.name: Nitrogen Dioxide (Dinitrogen Tetroxide)
chemicals.synonyms: Red fuming gas, Silo filler's gas, NO2 / N2O4
chemicals.symptoms: Coughing, chest tightness, methemoglobinemia, and biphasic DELAYED PULMONARY EDEMA (bronchiolitis obliterans) 6-24 hours post-exposure.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Strict bed rest + 24-hour observation. 2. 100% Oxygen. 3. Methylene Blue (1-2 mg/kg IV) if methemoglobinemia >20%.
chemicals.antidote: Methylene Blue IV for methemoglobinemia; high-dose corticosteroids for bronchiolitis.
chemicals.fire_response: Powerful oxidizer—ignites combustibles on contact. Reacts with water to form Nitric Acid.
chemicals.reactivity: Explodes with hydrocarbons, ammonia, hydrazine, nitrobenzene.
chemicals.storage_temp: Dedicated oxidizer gas cabinet
chemicals.sds_key_points: Distinctive heavy red-brown plume from nitric acid spills or agricultural grain silos.

chemicals.name: Organophosphate Pesticide (Parathion / Malathion / Chlorpyrifos)
chemicals.color: Pale yellow to dark brown liquid
chemicals.odor: Strong garlic / rotten cabbage mercaptan odor
chemicals.ppe_level: Level B Tychem/Butyl suit + SCBA (absorbs rapidly through intact skin and leather boots!)
chemicals.symptoms: CHOLINERGIC CRISIS (SLUDGEM / DUMBELS): Pinpoint pupils (miosis), profuse sweating, salivation, bronchorrhea ('drowning in secretions'), bradycardia, muscle fasciculations, seizures, respiratory arrest.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Strip clothing & wash skin with soap/water (rescuers MUST wear butyl/nitrile gloves!). 2. Administer ATROPINE (2-6 mg IV doubled every 5 min until lungs are dry) + PRALIDOXIME (2-PAM 1-2g IV)!
chemicals.antidote: Atropine Sulfate (titrated to dry bronchial secretions) + Pralidoxime (2-PAM) + Benzodiazepines (Midazolam).
chemicals.fire_response: Fight with foam, dry chemical, or CO2; dike all toxic agricultural runoff!
chemicals.reactivity: Hydrolyzes slowly in strong alkali; hydrocarbon carrier solvent is combustible.
chemicals.storage_temp: Locked ventilated agricultural pesticide shed with spill berm
chemicals.sds_key_points: Agricultural Pueblo/Arkansas Valley ranch hazard. Shares identical SLUDGEM presentation and Atropine+2-PAM antidote with Nerve Agents!

chemicals.name: Oxygen, Compressed
chemicals.synonyms: Gaseous Oxygen, O2 cylinder, Medical/Welding Oxygen
chemicals.symptoms: Accelerates combustion violently; oil or grease on regulator threads will explode (adiabatic diesel effect) when cylinder valve is opened!
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Air out oxygen-enriched clothing for 30 min.
chemicals.fire_response: Cool cylinders from cover; shut off oxygen supply to structure fires immediately.
chemicals.reactivity: NEVER apply oil, WD-40, or petroleum grease to an Oxygen regulator or valve!
chemicals.storage_temp: Chained upright minimum 20 ft from Acetylene/Propane or behind 5-ft fire barrier
chemicals.sds_key_points: Opening a high-pressure O2 valve with grease on the regulator causes an instant regulator explosion!

chemicals.name: Oxygen, Refrigerated Liquid (LOX)
chemicals.symptoms: Instant cryogenic freezing (-183C). Saturates clothing so a single spark turns garments into an unstoppable blowtorch!
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Air out oxygen-saturated clothing for 30+ minutes away from all sparks! 2. Thaw frostbite in warm water.
chemicals.fire_response: LOX spilled on ASPHALT, OIL, GREASE, OR WOOD forms a contact-sensitive HIGH EXPLOSIVE that detonates under footstep or vehicle tire impact!
chemicals.reactivity: Detonates when spilled on asphalt/bitumen or mixed with fuels/oil.
chemicals.storage_temp: Concrete pad ONLY (NEVER asphalt paving under LOX tanks!)
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Asphalt, oil, grease, flammable gases, wood
chemicals.sds_key_points: Hospital & welding bulk tank hazard. NEVER walk or drive on asphalt soaked with Liquid Oxygen!

chemicals.name: Paint or Paint Related Material (Solvent-Borne)
chemicals.synonyms: Enamel paint, Lacquer, Primer, Varnish, Auto body paint
chemicals.symptoms: Dizziness, headache, eye/skin irritation; two-part polyurethane paints contain Isocyanates causing severe occupational asthma!
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Fresh air. 2. Wash skin with soap & water.
chemicals.fire_response: Foam, CO2, dry chemical. Sealed paint cans explode when heated in structure fires.
chemicals.reactivity: Oil-based linseed/alkyd paint rags wad up and SPONTANEOUSLY COMBUST in trash cans due to exothermic oxidation!
chemicals.storage_temp: UL Flammable Cabinet; place oily rags in FM-approved self-closing oily waste can submerged in water
chemicals.sds_key_points: Linseed oil / stain rags spontaneously ignite within 2-6 hours if left wadded up!

chemicals.name: Paraquat Dichloride (Bipyridylium Herbicide)
chemicals.color: Dark blue-green dyed liquid (with stench & emetic added)
chemicals.symptoms: Oral burns, kidney/liver failure, followed by relentless, irreversible PULMONARY FIBROSIS (oxygen accelerates free-radical lung destruction!).
chemicals.first_aid: 1. CRITICAL RULE: DO NOT GIVE SUPPLEMENTAL OXYGEN unless PaO2 < 40 mmHg (SpO2 < 70%) because Oxygen fuels Paraquat free-radical lung destruction! 2. Give Fuller's Earth or Activated Charcoal immediately if ingested. 3. Scrub skin.
chemicals.antidote: Activated Charcoal / Fuller's Earth (1-2 g/kg orally within 1 hour) + Immunosuppression (Cyclophosphamide + Dexamethasone). WITHHOLD OXYGEN!
chemicals.fire_response: Non-flammable aqueous solution.
chemicals.reactivity: Corrosive to aluminum and zinc (evolves H2).
chemicals.storage_temp: Locked original container (never transfer to beverage bottles!)
chemicals.sds_key_points: CRITICAL EMS PARADOX: Paraquat is the ONE poison where giving 100% Oxygen accelerates fatal lung fibrosis! Keep SpO2 70-85%.

chemicals.name: Phenol, Solid or Molten (Carbolic Acid)
chemicals.color: White crystals turning pink/red in air
chemicals.odor: Distinctive sweet medicinal / tarry hospital odor
chemicals.respirator_req: Level A/B with SCBA + Butyl/Neoprene suit
chemicals.symptoms: ANESTHETIZES SKIN NERVES while causing deep white-to-brown gangrenous burns! Rapidly absorbed through small skin patches causing seizures, dark smoky urine, cardiac arrhythmia, and death within 30 minutes!
chemicals.first_aid: 1. WIPE SKIN IMMEDIATELY WITH POLYETHYLENE GLYCOL 300/400 (PEG) OR ISOPROPYL ALCOHOL / HIGH-FLOW WATER! (Low-volume water spreads phenol absorption!). 2. High-flow oxygen & ECG monitoring.
chemicals.fire_response: Combustible solid/liquid. Use alcohol-resistant foam, CO2, dry chemical.
chemicals.reactivity: Reacts violently with calcium hypochlorite, nitric acid, aluminum chloride.
chemicals.storage_temp: Locked poison cabinet with PEG-300 decon kit mounted outside
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Oxidizers, calcium hypochlorite, nitric acid, strong bases
chemicals.sds_key_points: Unique decon rule: Use Polyethylene Glycol (PEG-300/400) or deluge-volume water; small amounts of water increase dermal fatality!

chemicals.name: Phosgene
chemicals.synonyms: Carbonyl chloride, CG Warfare Agent, COCl2
chemicals.color: Colorless to pale yellow fuming gas
chemicals.odor: Newly mown hay or green corn at low ppm; suffocating pungent at high ppm
chemicals.respirator_req: Level A fully encapsulating suit + SCBA
chemicals.symptoms: Minimal initial irritation followed by LATENT DELAYED PULMONARY EDEMA 2 to 24 hours later! Severe dyspnea, frothy sputum, hypovolemic shock, death.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Enforce strict bed rest and 24-hour ICU observation even if asymptomatic! 2. Oxygen + PEEP/CPAP. 3. Flush eyes/skin.
chemicals.antidote: Nebulized N-acetylcysteine, high-dose inhaled/IV corticosteroids, PEEP ventilation.
chemicals.fire_response: Non-flammable gas. Water reacts slowly to form HCl and CO2; use fog upwind to knock down plume.
chemicals.reactivity: Generated accidentally when chlorinated brake cleaner (Tetrachloroethylene) or refrigerants contact welding arcs or hot exhaust manifolds!
chemicals.storage_temp: Negative-pressure toxic gas vault with caustic scrubber
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Water, ammonia, amines, alcohols, welding arcs near chlorinated solvents
chemicals.sds_key_points: Deadly 24-hour delayed lung edema trap. Generated in auto shops when welding over brake cleaner!

chemicals.name: Phosphoric Acid, Solution
chemicals.synonyms: Orthophosphoric acid, Naval Jelly rust remover, H3PO4
chemicals.symptoms: Severe eye burns, skin irritation/burns, coughing from mist.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Flush eyes/skin 15 min with water. 2. Dilute with water if ingested; do not induce vomiting.
chemicals.fire_response: Non-flammable, but liberates flammable Hydrogen gas on contact with mild steel/zinc.
chemicals.reactivity: Incompatible with strong bases, sodium tetrahydroborate, chlorates.
chemicals.storage_temp: Polyethylene acid storage above 15C (crystallizes in cold)
chemicals.sds_key_points: Found in commercial rust converters, restaurant sanitizers, and beverage syrup concentrates.

chemicals.name: Phosphorus Trichloride
chemicals.symptoms: Violently reacts with tear/airway moisture to form Hydrochloric Acid and Phosphorous Acid, causing deep burns and fatal pulmonary edema.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Move upwind. 2. Blot excess liquid before deluging with massive water. 3. 24-hour ICU lung observation.
chemicals.fire_response: DO NOT apply water directly into liquid spill (explosive evolution of HCl gas and spontaneously flammable Phosphine PH3!). Cover spill with dry sand or soda ash.
chemicals.reactivity: Explodes with water, nitric acid, sodium, potassium, and organic matter.
chemicals.storage_temp: Dry hermetically sealed drum in water-free vault
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Water, humid air, acids, bases, alcohols, metals
chemicals.sds_key_points: ERG Table 1 TIH (Toxic Inhalation Hazard) chemical—violently water-reactive!

chemicals.name: Phosphorus, White or Yellow
chemicals.odor: Garlic-like odor; dense white P2O5 smoke
chemicals.symptoms: IGNITES SPONTANEOUSLY IN AIR AT 30C (86F)! Particles embedded in skin continue burning through muscle to bone and re-ignite whenever exposed to air! Systemic phosphorus absorption causes fatal hypocalcemia and liver failure.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. KEEP WOUNDS SUBMERGED IN WATER OR COVERED WITH WET SALINE DRESSINGS! 2. Use UV Wood's lamp in dark room to see fluorescent particles and remove with metal forceps (never fingers!). 3. Flush with 1% Copper Sulfate (turns particles black) + Sodium Bicarbonate.
chemicals.antidote: Continuous water immersion + UV Wood's lamp debridement + IV Calcium Gluconate for hypocalcemia.
chemicals.fire_response: Deluge with water and cover with wet sand/mud, then drum under water. Re-ignites as soon as water dries!
chemicals.reactivity: Explodes on contact with oxidizers, halogens, and hot alkalis (forms deadly Phosphine gas PH3!).
chemicals.storage_temp: Submerged under water in double-sealed metal drum away from freeze/heat
chemicals.sds_key_points: Unique rule: White Phosphorus is stored UNDER WATER and re-ignites the instant it dries out in air!

chemicals.name: Potassium Chlorate
chemicals.synonyms: Chlorate of potash, Pyrotechnic oxidizer, KClO3
chemicals.symptoms: Methemoglobinemia (chocolate-brown blood, cyanosis unresponsive to O2), hemolysis, acute renal failure if ingested.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Flush eyes/skin. 2. Methylene Blue IV for methemoglobinemia.
chemicals.antidote: Methylene Blue (1-2 mg/kg IV) + exchange transfusion if severe hemolysis.
chemicals.fire_response: Flood with massive water from cover (dry chemical and CO2 are ineffective because chlorate supplies its own oxygen!).
chemicals.reactivity: Detonates from friction or impact when mixed with sulfur, sugar, charcoal, red phosphorus, ammonium salts, or sulfuric acid!
chemicals.storage_temp: Dedicated oxidizer cabinet isolated from acids, ammonium salts, and combustibles
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Sulfuric acid, ammonium salts, sulfur, sugar, metal powders, organic fuels
chemicals.sds_key_points: Match-head & fireworks oxidizer. Friction-sensitive explosive when contaminated with any fuel or ammonium salt!

chemicals.name: Potassium Hydroxide, Solution (Caustic Potash)
chemicals.color: Colorless liquid or white deliquescent pellets
chemicals.ppe_level: Face shield, neoprene gloves, rubber apron
chemicals.symptoms: Deep liquefactive caustic burns, permanent blindness, severe airway burns.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Irrigate continuously with water for 30+ minutes. 2. Immediate ophthalmology consult for eye splashes.
chemicals.fire_response: Attacks aluminum and zinc to evolve explosive H2 gas.
chemicals.reactivity: Violent heat release with acids and water.
chemicals.storage_temp: Airtight HDPE container in Base cabinet
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Acids, aluminum, magnesium, zinc, halogenated hydrocarbons
chemicals.sds_key_points: Used in alkaline batteries, biodiesel transesterification, and liquid soaps.

chemicals.name: Propane (LPG / Liquefied Petroleum Gas)
chemicals.odor: Rotten cabbage / mercaptan odorant added (pure is odorless)
chemicals.respirator_req: SCBA in oxygen-deficient or high-vapor zones
chemicals.ppe_level: Structural bunker gear + SCBA; thermal gloves for liquid leak
chemicals.symptoms: Asphyxiation in low areas (vapor heavier than air), CNS dizziness, severe cryogenic frostbite from liquid spray, catastrophic flash fire.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Move upwind; avoid low-lying vapor pockets. 2. Warm frostbite with lukewarm water. 3. High-flow oxygen.
chemicals.fire_response: BLEVE HAZARD! Cool tank shells with unmanned master streams from minimum 500m if flames impinge on vapor space. Do not extinguish leak unless flow can be shut off immediately.
chemicals.reactivity: Explosive with oxidizers, chlorine dioxide. Vapors hug ground and travel to ignition sources.
chemicals.storage_temp: Outdoor ventilated cylinder rack away from sun/sparks
chemicals.sds_key_points: I-25 / US-50 highway tanker & rural ranch tank staple. Immediate BLEVE evacuation 1 mile (1600m) if tank is whistling or discoloring.

chemicals.name: R-1234yf Automotive Refrigerant (2,3,3,3-Tetrafluoropropene)
chemicals.ppe_level: Turnout gear + SCBA (emits lethal HF in engine compartment fires!)
chemicals.symptoms: Cryogenic frostbite from liquid; in vehicle fires (2016+ cars), R-1234yf burns and decomposes into concentrated HYDROFLUORIC ACID (HF) and Carbonyl Fluoride!
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Move upwind of burning vehicle smoke. 2. Treat smoke/acid exposure with Calcium Gluconate.
chemicals.antidote: Calcium Gluconate (2.5% nebulized or topical gel) for HF exposure from burning AC lines.
chemicals.fire_response: Flammable gas (unlike older R-134a). Vehicle engine fires rupture AC lines and release toxic HF gas—SCBA mandatory during all car fires!
chemicals.reactivity: Incompatible with oxidizers, alkali metals, finely divided aluminum.
chemicals.storage_temp: Cool cylinder rack (<50C) in auto bay
chemicals.sds_key_points: Standard in 2016+ vehicles. Flammable A2L refrigerant that generates Hydrofluoric Acid (HF) during car fires!

chemicals.name: R-134a Automotive Refrigerant
chemicals.ppe_level: Safety glasses with side shields, thermal insulating gloves
chemicals.symptoms: Liquid contact causes instant cryogenic frostbite / tissue freezing. High concentrations in pits cause rapid asphyxiation and cardiac arrhythmia.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Move to fresh air. 2. Warm frostbitten areas in lukewarm water (do not rub). 3. Administer oxygen. 4. Avoid epinephrine.
chemicals.fire_response: Non-flammable at ambient conditions, but containers rupture explosively in fire. High heat breaks down gas into toxic HYDROFLUORIC ACID (HF) and CARBONYL FLUORIDE.
chemicals.reactivity: Incompatible with alkali metals (magnesium, aluminum shavings), potassium.
chemicals.storage_temp: Cool, dry area (<50°C). Tightly secure cylinders.
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Active metals, open flames, intense heat
chemicals.sds_key_points: Standard automotive AC recharge can. Heavy gas displaces air in auto inspection pits.

chemicals.name: Ricin Toxin (Castor Bean Biotoxin)
chemicals.respirator_req: Level A/B with PAPR/SCBA (P100 filter captures non-volatile protein)
chemicals.ppe_level: Level B Tychem suit + SCBA or PAPR with P100
chemicals.symptoms: Ribosome-inactivating toxin: 4-8h after inhalation causes fever, cough, necrotizing pulmonary edema, and respiratory failure; ingestion causes bloody diarrhea and multi-organ failure.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Wet down powder with 0.5% bleach + soap (inactivates protein and prevents re-aerosolization). 2. Scrub skin with soap and water. 3. Aggressive ICU supportive care.
chemicals.fire_response: Heat (>80C for 10 min) and 0.5% sodium hypochlorite bleach denature and destroy Ricin protein.
chemicals.reactivity: Inactivated by heat and hypochlorite bleach.
chemicals.storage_temp: BSL-3 Select Agent security
chemicals.sds_key_points: Non-contagious biological toxin extracted from castor bean mash. Destroyed by 0.5% bleach or >80C heat.

chemicals.name: Sarin (GB)
chemicals.odor: Odorless in pure form; faint fruity odor if impure
chemicals.respirator_req: Level A CBRN SCBA strictly mandatory
chemicals.symptoms: SLUDGEM: Pinpoint pupils, profuse salivation, lacrimation, urination, defecation, seizures, respiratory arrest
chemicals.first_aid: 1. LEVEL A RESCUE. 2. Immediate Atropine + 2-PAM (MARK I / ATNAA auto-injector). 3. Midazolam for seizures. 4. Decon with 0.5% bleach.
chemicals.fire_response: CBRN HazMat / Military EOD required.
chemicals.reactivity: Neutralized by bleach and sodium hydroxide.
chemicals.storage_temp: High-security bunker storage
chemicals.sds_key_points: CBRN chemical warfare nerve agent. Rapid lethality.

chemicals.name: Sodium (Metallic Sodium)
chemicals.ppe_level: Flame-resistant apron, face shield, dry leather/butyl gloves + SCBA
chemicals.symptoms: Reacts violently with skin moisture causing simultaneous thermal burns and deep caustic NaOH burns!
chemicals.first_aid: 1. WIPE OR BRUSH OFF ALL METAL PARTICLES WITH DRY MINERAL OIL OR FORCEPS BEFORE APPLYING WATER! 2. Once metal is removed, flood caustic burn with water for 30 min.
chemicals.antidote: Mineral oil mechanical removal followed by copious water deluge.
chemicals.fire_response: NEVER USE WATER, FOAM, CO2, OR HALON! Use Class D Dry Powder (Met-L-X, Na-X, dry soda ash, or bone-dry sand).
chemicals.reactivity: Explodes on contact with water, ice, acids, halogens, and chlorinated solvents (Brake Cleaner).
chemicals.storage_temp: Submerged in anhydrous mineral oil / kerosene inside waterproof Class D locker
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Water, moisture, acids, CO2, chlorinated solvents, halogens
chemicals.sds_key_points: Never use water or CO2 extinguishers on Sodium metal fires!

chemicals.name: Sodium Chlorate
chemicals.ppe_level: Goggles, rubber boots/gloves (NEVER cotton clothes—solution dried on clothes ignites by friction!)
chemicals.symptoms: Methemoglobinemia, hemolysis, renal failure; clothing splashed with solution dries into an explosive fuse!
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Strip splashed clothing immediately and soak in water! 2. Methylene Blue IV for methemoglobinemia.
chemicals.fire_response: Flood with water from distance.
chemicals.reactivity: Explodes with acids (forms Chlorine Dioxide ClO2 gas), ammonium salts, sulfur, and organic matter.
chemicals.storage_temp: Cool dry oxidizer storage
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Acids, ammonium compounds, organic matter, wood/cotton
chemicals.sds_key_points: Spilled solution dried on wood pallets or cotton uniforms ignites from the friction of walking!

chemicals.name: Sodium Cyanide, Solid
chemicals.odor: Faint bitter almond odor when damp
chemicals.symptoms: Rapid cellular hypoxia, confusion, seizures, cherry-red skin, severe metabolic acidosis, cardiac arrest within minutes.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Remove from exposure with SCBA. 2. Brush off powder & wash skin. 3. Administer CYANOKIT (Hydroxocobalamin 5g IV) immediately!
chemicals.antidote: Hydroxocobalamin (Cyanokit 5g IV) or Sodium Nitrite + Sodium Thiosulfate.
chemicals.fire_response: Do NOT use CO2 extinguishers or acidic water (CO2 + moisture forms carbonic acid, liberating HCN gas)! Use dry alkali powder.
chemicals.reactivity: Contact with ANY acid, acid fumes, or even weakly acidic water releases lethal Hydrogen Cyanide (HCN) gas.
chemicals.storage_temp: Locked double-contained cyanide vault kept strictly alkaline (pH > 11)
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: All acids, CO2 fire extinguishers, nitrites, chlorates
chemicals.sds_key_points: Mining & electroplating staple in Colorado. Never use CO2 extinguishers on cyanide fires!

chemicals.name: Sodium Hydroxide, Solution (Caustic Soda / Lye)
chemicals.synonyms: Lye, Liquid Plumber, Oven cleaner, NaOH
chemicals.color: Clear soapy-feeling liquid or white pellets
chemicals.respirator_req: N95/P100 for dust/mist; SCBA above 10 mg/m3
chemicals.ppe_level: Chemical goggles, face shield, butyl/neoprene gloves
chemicals.symptoms: LIQUEFACTIVE NECROSIS: Saponifies skin fats (feels slippery/soapy while dissolving deep tissue!), rapid permanent corneal blindness, esophageal perforation.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Brush off dry pellets, then flush continuously with water for 30 to 60 minutes until soapy feel is gone! 2. Never induce vomiting or give acids to neutralize!
chemicals.fire_response: Non-flammable, but reacts with Aluminum, Zinc, and Tin to generate explosive HYDROGEN GAS (H2)!
chemicals.reactivity: Violent exothermic reaction with acids, water (when dissolving solid pellets), and nitro-organics.
chemicals.storage_temp: Corrosive Base cabinet (keep away from Aluminum & Acids)
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Acids, aluminum, zinc, tin, trichlorethylene (forms explosive dichloroacetylene!)
chemicals.sds_key_points: Mixing Lye with Trichloroethylene forms spontaneously explosive Dichloroacetylene gas!

chemicals.name: Sodium Peroxide (Inorganic Peroxide Oxidizer)
chemicals.ppe_level: Face shield, butyl gloves, flame-resistant apron
chemicals.symptoms: Severe caustic burns on contact with moist skin/eyes.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Brush off dry powder before flooding with massive water for 30 min.
chemicals.antidote: Water deluge after brushing dry powder.
chemicals.fire_response: Reacts violently with water to liberate Oxygen and Caustic Soda heat—spontaneously ignites paper, wood, or organics on contact with a single drop of water!
chemicals.reactivity: Spontaneous explosion with acetic acid, alcohols, glycerol, sulfur, aluminum powder, or damp wood.
chemicals.storage_temp: Airtight metal drum in dry oxidizer locker
chemicals.storage_incompatibilities: Water, organic matter, alcohols, acids, metal powders
chemicals.sds_key_points: Ignites paper or wood instantly if dampened with a drop of water!

chemicals.name: Styrene Monomer, Stabilized
chemicals.synonyms: Vinylbenzene, Phenylethene, Fiberglass boat resin monomer
chemicals.odor: Sweet floral odor at low ppm; sharp disagreeable fiberglass odor at high ppm
chemicals.ppe_level: PVA or Viton gloves + splash goggles
chemicals.symptoms: Styrene sickness: headache, fatigue, dizziness, central & peripheral neuropathy, severe eye irritation.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Fresh air. 2. Flush eyes/skin with soap and water.
chemicals.fire_response: RUNAWAY POLYMERIZATION HAZARD if heated above 65C or if TBC inhibitor is depleted! Cool tanks from unmanned position.
chemicals.reactivity: Polymerizes violently with peroxides, strong acids, aluminum chloride, or heat.
chemicals.storage_temp: Cool (<25C) ventilated monomer storage; check TBC inhibitor level monthly
chemicals.sds_key_points: Used in cultured marble, fiberglass tub/auto fabrication, and plastics manufacturing.

chemicals.name: Sulfur Dioxide
chemicals.odor: Strong suffocating burning match / sulfur odor
chemicals.ppe_level: Level A or Level B + SCBA
chemicals.symptoms: Immediate choking, laryngospasm, severe bronchospasm, corneal burns, frostbite from liquid release.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Move upwind. 2. Irrigate eyes/skin 15 min. 3. Humidified oxygen + bronchodilators (albuterol).
chemicals.fire_response: Non-flammable. Reacts with water to form corrosive sulfurous acid.
chemicals.reactivity: Violent reaction with alkali metals, ammonia, chlorates, powdered metals.
chemicals.storage_temp: Cool ventilated cylinder bay
chemicals.sds_key_points: Heavy gas (VD 2.26) settles in valleys and rail yards.

chemicals.name: Sulfur Mustard (Mustard Gas / Blister Agent HD)
chemicals.color: Yellow to dark brown oily liquid
chemicals.symptoms: 2 to 24 HOUR ASYMPTOMATIC LATENT PERIOD followed by excruciating large fluid-filled blisters, corneal blindness, airway pseudomembranes, and bone marrow suppression (leukopenia)!
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Immediate decontamination within 2 minutes of contact using RSDL, Dry Blot (Fuller's Earth), or 0.5% Bleach! 2. Burn-center fluid management.
chemicals.antidote: No systemic chemical antidote (Sodium Thiosulfate IV within 20 min may reduce alkylation; supportive burn & G-CSF marrow care).
chemicals.fire_response: CBRN HazMat protocol; decomposes to HCl and SO2 in fire.
chemicals.reactivity: Reacts vigorously with bleach/hypochlorites (neutralizes agent but generates heat).
chemicals.storage_temp: CBRN containment
chemicals.sds_key_points: Alkylation damage occurs within 2 minutes of skin contact even though blisters take hours to appear!

chemicals.name: Sulfur, Molten
chemicals.color: Amber molten liquid; yellow solid crust
chemicals.odor: Rotten eggs (H2S) in tank headspace; choking SO2 when burning
chemicals.symptoms: Severe thermal burns from molten sulfur; burns with pale blue flame releasing suffocating Sulfur Dioxide (SO2); tank headspace holds lethal H2S!
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Cool molten sulfur burn with water—do NOT pull off solidified sulfur crust.
chemicals.fire_response: Use fine water fog or steam (avoid solid water streams into molten pool—steam eruption).
chemicals.reactivity: Forms explosive gunpowder mixtures with chlorates, nitrates, and oxidizers.
chemicals.storage_temp: Heated insulated rail car / dry sulfur bin away from oxidizers
chemicals.sds_key_points: Common rail car cargo through Pueblo.

chemicals.name: Sulfuric Acid, Concentrated (>51%)
chemicals.color: Clear colorless to dark brown oily liquid
chemicals.odor: Odorless cold; choking sulfur trioxide fumes when hot
chemicals.respirator_req: SCBA or Acid Gas + P100 full facepiece
chemicals.ppe_level: Level B Acid Splash Suit + Viton/Butyl gloves
chemicals.symptoms: Immediate charring third-degree chemical burns (dehydrates tissue carbon), blindness, severe pulmonary edema from mist.
chemicals.first_aid: 1. Brush off excess if oleum, then deluge with massive volume of water for 30 min. 2. Never induce vomiting.
chemicals.antidote: Aggressive water deluge; calcium carbonate / sodium bicarbonate for spill neutralization.
chemicals.fire_response: NEVER pour water into concentrated sulfuric acid (explosive steam splatter)! Attacks metals to release explosive Hydrogen gas.
